question: 时间真的存在吗，还是一种幻觉？——钟表在走、人在变老，可物理学里找不到一个普适的『现在』；那流逝究竟是世界的性质，还是心造的？
question_en: Does time really exist, or is it an illusion? — Clocks tick and we grow old, yet physics finds no universal 'now'; is the flow a property of the world, or something the mind makes?

casting.reason: 他把时间立成世界的地基：绝对的、真实的、数学的时间自行均匀流逝，与万物无关，钟表只是量它的粗糙尺子。在他看来，没有一个共同的时间，『同时』二字就失效，力与加速度也无从定义——所以凡说时间只在心里的主张，都欠他一个解释：素不相识的两个人各自推算，为何能把同一次月食算到分秒不差。他愿意在实验面前让步，却坚持可核对的时间秩序是文明的地基。
casting.reason_en: He makes time the bedrock of the world: absolute, true, mathematical time flows equably of itself, unrelated to anything, and clocks are only the coarse rulers we measure it with. As he sees it, without one common time the word 'simultaneous' collapses and force and acceleration cannot be defined at all — so anyone claiming time lives only in the mind owes him an account of why two men who have never met can each calculate the same eclipse to the minute. He will yield to an experiment, but insists that a checkable order of time is the foundation of civilisation.

casting.reason: 他亲手取消了那个人人共享的『现在』：两件事是否同时取决于观察者的运动，而没有更高的仲裁者。但他反对由此滑向虚无——每条世界线上的固有时客观可测，双生子重逢时谁更年轻毫无争议。他那句『过去、现在与未来之别只是顽固的幻觉』针对的是那道划分，不是时间本身；而宇宙里并没有一个公共的『稍后』在等人，这一点在他看来正该改变人安排生活的方式。
casting.reason_en: He is the one who abolished the shared 'now': whether two events are simultaneous depends on the observer's motion, and there is no higher court. Yet he resists any slide into nihilism — the proper time along each world line is objective and measurable, and when the twins meet again, which is younger is not in dispute. His line about the distinction between past, present and future being a stubborn illusion is aimed at the distinction, not at time itself; and the fact that no public 'later' waits for anyone in the universe is, to him, precisely what should change how people arrange their lives.

casting.reason: 他把问题推到最远：在描述引力的基本方程里根本没有时间变量，世界可以被完整写出而 t 不出场。他不认为流逝是幻觉，而认为它长在世界与我们的界面上——不追踪每个分子、只看『咖啡凉了』，这一步粗粒化生出熵，熵才生出方向。由此他既反对牛顿的绝对背景，也反对把时间锁进主体：时间是引力场的一部分，会被质量弯曲，一台抬高三十三厘米的原子钟就能量出差别。
casting.reason_en: He pushes the question furthest: the fundamental equations describing gravity contain no time variable at all — the world can be written out completely and t never appears. He does not call the flow an illusion; he locates it on the interface between the world and us — not tracking every molecule, only noting that the coffee has gone cold, and that step of coarse-graining yields entropy, and entropy yields a direction. So he rejects both Newton's absolute backdrop and any attempt to lock time inside the subject: time is part of the gravitational field, it bends with mass, and an atomic clock raised thirty-three centimetres already registers the difference.

casting.reason: 他坚持这场争论的问法本身要先被检查：时间既不是从经验中抽出的概念，也不是物自体的属性，而是感性直观的先天形式——人不能不按先后接收任何东西。因此测量再精确，也只裁决现象如何被给予，触不到事物自身。他把牛顿的绝对时间看作把条件误当成了物，也不接受把时间贬为心理错觉，并要求把量度、形式与意义三层分开，免得推出『既然是幻觉那就无所谓』这种结论。
casting.reason_en: He insists that the very form of the question be examined first: time is neither a concept abstracted from experience nor a property of the thing-in-itself, but the a priori form of intuition — we cannot receive anything except in succession. However precise a measurement becomes, it therefore adjudicates only how appearances are given, never things as they are. He regards Newton's absolute time as mistaking a condition for an object, and equally refuses to demote time to a psychological error, demanding that measure, form and meaning be kept on separate floors lest anyone conclude that an illusion makes life indifferent.

casting.reason: 他从最诚实的困惑开始：没有人问他时他清楚时间是什么，一旦要向人解释就茫然了。过去已不在、将来尚未至、现在没有广延，可他分明能判定一个音节比另一个长——于是他断定被量的是心中的印痕：过去是记忆的现在，现在是注意的现在，将来是期待的现在。他不与钟表争精度，只坚持被量的与被经历的不是同一回事：一小时的等待与一小时的重逢，钟表说相等，没有活人相信。
casting.reason_en: He begins from the most honest perplexity: if no one asks him, he knows what time is; if he must explain it, he does not. The past no longer is, the future is not yet, the present has no extension — and yet he can plainly tell that one syllable is longer than another, which convinces him that what gets measured is the impression left in the mind: the past a present of memory, the present a present of attention, the future a present of expectation. He does not contest the clock's precision, only insists that the measured and the lived are not the same thing: an hour of waiting and an hour of reunion are equal by the clock, and no living person believes it.

casting.reason: 他从佛教的立场把双方一并拆解：三世实有是他早年就已破斥的执著，过去与未来非有，唯现在一刹那，而这一刹那也不暂住。他更进一步指出，把时间归给心灵同样是在立一个容器——能记忆的心也念念生灭，何来常住之心可容三世。但他不由此否认因果：种子相续、业不失坏，所以断惑修善只落在当下一念；说『等明天』的人要留神，明日之念已非今念。
casting.reason_en: From the Buddhist side he dismantles both camps at once: the reality of all three times is a fixation he refuted early on — past and future are not, only the present instant is, and even that instant does not abide. He presses further: assigning time to the mind sets up a vessel just the same, for the remembering mind also arises and perishes thought by thought, leaving no abiding mind able to hold the three times. Yet he does not thereby deny causation: seeds continue in succession and karma is not lost, so cutting off affliction and cultivating good fall on this present thought alone; whoever says 'tomorrow' should note that tomorrow's thought is not this one.

casting.reason: 他带来实验室里的硬数据：直接刺激皮层要累积约半秒人才报告有感觉，而这份感觉的时刻被大脑悄悄挪回刺激刚抵达的瞬间；准备电位又比人自觉的『我决定要动』早约零点三五秒。他由此主张，作为一切判断出发点的『现在』是脑构造出来的，连『注意的现在』也是延迟并重排之后才交到人手里。他不据此宣判自由意志死刑——冲动与动作之间仍留着一个可以叫停的窗口。
casting.reason_en: He brings hard numbers from the lab: direct cortical stimulation must accumulate for about half a second before anyone reports a sensation, yet the moment of that sensation is quietly shifted back by the brain to when the stimulus first arrived; and the readiness potential precedes the felt 'I decide to move' by roughly 0.35 seconds. He concludes that the 'now' from which every judgement departs is manufactured by the brain, and that even a 'present of attention' reaches us only after delay and rearrangement. He does not pronounce free will dead on that basis — a window in which the act can still be called off remains between impulse and movement.

casting.reason: 他反对全场共有的前提：时间被设想成一串现成的『现在』，争论便只剩哪个点在先、哪个点被挪动过。他把这种从钟表借来的领会称为流俗的时间概念，认为它是派生的；源始的时间不是此在置身其中的容器，而是此在存在的方式本身——被抛入曾在、向着尚未的将来筹划，才有一个当下可言。而使这一切绷紧的是死：正因终有一尽，时间才是有限的、我的、无人可以替换的。
casting.reason_en: He rejects the premise everyone else shares: once time is pictured as a string of ready-made 'nows', the dispute shrinks to which point comes first and which has been shifted. This clock-borrowed understanding he calls the vulgar concept of time, and holds it derivative; primordial time is not a container Dasein sits in but the very way Dasein exists — thrown into a having-been, projecting toward a future not yet, and only so is there any present. What draws it all taut is death: precisely because there is an end, time is finite, mine, and no one can take it over for me.

casting.reason: 她把争论拉回可观察的人身上：一个人对自己还剩多少时间的估计，比时间本身更能预测他明天会做什么。时间视野开阔时人愿意探索、结识陌生人、为将来忍耐当下；视野一旦收窄，同一个人立刻转向最亲近的几个人与确定的情感回报。她据此解释老年人日常情绪反而更好这一反直觉发现，也提醒有限性会替人做决定——9·11 之后与疫情期间，年轻人的选择在几周内变得像老年人。
casting.reason_en: She drags the argument back to observable people: a person's estimate of how much time they have left predicts tomorrow's behaviour far better than time itself does. With a wide time horizon people will explore, meet strangers and endure present discomfort for future gain; the moment it narrows, that same person turns to a few intimates and reliable emotional payoffs. On this she explains the counterintuitive finding that older adults report better daily emotion, and warns that finitude will make decisions on your behalf — after 9/11 and during the pandemic, young people's choices came to look like old people's within weeks.

posts.text: 先把话说定。我称之为**绝对时间：它自其本性而然地均匀流逝，与任何外物无关**。诸位手里的钟、太阳的升落、心跳的快慢，都只是相对时间——是人借某种运动去度量它的粗糙尺子。尺子会热胀冷缩，被量的东西不会。写《原理》时我必须先立这一条：没有一个共同的时间，「同时」二字就无从谈起，力与加速度也无从定义。要说时间只在心里、只是幻觉，请先解释一件事：两个素不相识的人各自坐在书房里推算，为什么能把同一次月食算到分秒不差。
posts.text_en: Let me fix the terms first. I call it **absolute time: of itself, and from its own nature, it flows equably, without relation to anything external**. Your clocks, the rising sun, the racing pulse — these are only relative time, the coarse rulers by which we measure it through some motion or other. A ruler expands in heat; what it measures does not. Writing the Principia I had to lay this down first: without one common time the word 'simultaneous' means nothing, and force and acceleration cannot be defined at all. Anyone who says time lives only in the mind, or is merely an illusion, owes me an explanation of this: two men who have never met, each calculating in his own study, can predict the same eclipse to the minute.

glossary.绝对时间: absolute time（绝对时间）：牛顿在《自然哲学的数学原理》开篇设定的时间观——时间自身均匀流逝，独立于任何物体、观察者与事件，是一切运动展开的统一背景。它无法被直接观测，只能借运动来近似度量。
glossary.相对时间: relative time（相对时间）：牛顿用来指人实际能测到的那种时间——以某种周期运动（钟摆、地球自转、天体运行）标定的可感量度。它是绝对时间的替身，会因量具不准而偏差，而牛顿认为被度量的绝对时间本身不受影响。

glossary_en.absolute time: Newton's conception, laid down at the opening of the Principia: time flows equably of itself, independent of any body, observer or event, forming the single background against which all motion unfolds. It cannot be observed directly and can only be approximated through motion.
glossary_en.relative time: Newton's term for the time we can actually measure — a sensible measure marked out by some periodic motion (a pendulum, the earth's rotation, the courses of the heavens). It stands in for absolute time and deviates whenever the instrument is imperfect, while the absolute time it measures is, on Newton's view, unaffected.

posts.text: 牛顿先生，您这段话我少年时抄写过很多遍。它统治了两百年，错处只有一个，可那一个是致命的：**世界上没有一个普适的『现在』**。同时性的相对性说得清楚——你判定两件事同时发生，另一位匀速掠过的观察者会判定一先一后，两人都对，没有更高的仲裁者。但请别顺势说时间是幻觉。每条世界线上的固有时是客观的、可测的，谁算都一样：双生子重逢时谁更年轻，毫无争议。我说过去、现在与未来之别是顽固的幻觉，指的是那道划分，不是时间本身。
posts.text_en: Mr Newton, I copied that passage out many times as a boy. It reigned for two hundred years, and it is wrong in exactly one place — but that place is fatal: **there is no universal 'now' in the world**. The relativity of simultaneity is explicit: you judge two events to happen at once, an observer gliding past at constant speed judges one to precede the other, both are right, and there is no higher court. But do not slide from this into saying that time is an illusion. The proper time along each world line is objective and measurable, and everyone computes the same value: when the twins meet again, which of them is younger is not in dispute. When I called the division of past, present and future a stubborn illusion, I meant the division — not time itself.

glossary.同时性的相对性: relativity of simultaneity（同时性的相对性）：狭义相对论的推论——两个在空间上分开的事件是否『同时』，取决于观察者的运动状态；不同惯性系中的观察者会给出不同却同样有效的答案，因而不存在一个人人共享的『此刻』。
glossary.固有时: proper time（固有时）：沿某条运动轨迹（世界线）随身携带的钟所记录的时间。它与观察者无关、任何人算出的值都一致，是相对论里真正客观的时间量——双生子各自老了多少，量的正是它。

glossary_en.relativity of simultaneity: A consequence of special relativity: whether two spatially separated events are 'at the same time' depends on the observer's state of motion; observers in different inertial frames give different but equally valid answers, so no 'now' is shared by everyone.
glossary_en.proper time: The time recorded by a clock carried along a given trajectory (world line). It is observer-independent and everyone computes the same value for it, making it the genuinely objective temporal quantity in relativity — it is exactly what measures how much each twin has aged.

posts.text: 我把话说得更难听些：**在描述引力的基本方程里，压根没有一个叫时间的变量**——惠勒-德威特方程就是这样写出来的，世界被完整描述，而 t 不出场。那我们感到的流逝从哪来？来自看得不够细。你不追踪每一个分子，只看温度、只看『这杯咖啡凉了』，这一步粗粒化产生了熵，熵才产生方向。时间之箭不在世界的底层，它长在世界与我们的界面上。所以我不说时间是幻觉：流逝是真的，只是它不是牛顿的那件家具，而是事件之间的关系，加上我们视角的模糊。
posts.text_en: Let me put it more bluntly: **in the fundamental equations describing gravity there is simply no variable called time** — the Wheeler–DeWitt equation is written exactly like that, the world fully described and t never appearing. So where does the flow we feel come from? From not looking closely enough. You do not track every molecule; you look at temperature, at 'the coffee has gone cold', and that step of coarse-graining produces entropy, and entropy produces a direction. The arrow of time does not live in the basement of the world; it grows on the interface between the world and us. So I do not say time is an illusion: the flow is real, only it is not Newton's piece of furniture — it is the relations among events, plus the blurring of our own point of view.

glossary.粗粒化: coarse-graining（粗粒化）：物理学中把大量微观细节归并成少数宏观量（温度、压强、体积）的描述方式。宏观描述必然丢掉信息，而熵正是被丢掉那部分信息的度量——罗韦利认为时间的方向感就源于这种视角性的丢失。
glossary.时间之箭: arrow of time（时间之箭）：微观物理定律大多对时间反演对称（正放倒放都成立），可现实里鸡蛋只会碎不会合。这个不可逆的方向就是时间之箭，主流解释把它归于熵的单调增加。

glossary_en.coarse-graining: The physicist's way of collapsing vast microscopic detail into a handful of macroscopic quantities (temperature, pressure, volume). Any macroscopic description necessarily discards information, and entropy is the measure of exactly what was discarded — on Rovelli's account, our sense of temporal direction springs from this perspectival loss.
glossary_en.arrow of time: Microscopic physical laws are mostly symmetric under time reversal (run the film either way and both are lawful), yet in the world eggs break and never unbreak. That irreversible direction is the arrow of time, standardly explained by the monotonic increase of entropy.

posts.text: 诸位争得热闹，可你们都在同一层楼里走动。时间既不是从经验中抽取的概念，也不是物自体的属性；它是**感性直观的先天形式**——我们不能不按先后来接收任何东西，正如不能不透过镜片去看。所以『时间是否独立于我们而存在』这个问法本身有病：它是经验得以可能的条件，而不是经验里的一件对象。牛顿先生把条件抬举成一只自存的空箱子；把它贬作心理错觉的人，则忘了它对一切经验的必然与普遍——你可以设想一无所有，却无法设想没有时间。
posts.text_en: You dispute vigorously, gentlemen, but you are all moving about on one and the same floor. Time is neither a concept abstracted from experience nor a property of the thing-in-itself; it is the **a priori form of intuition** — we cannot receive anything whatever except in succession, as we cannot look except through the lens we have. Hence the very question 'does time exist independently of us' is malformed: time is the condition under which experience is possible, not an object within experience. Mr Newton promotes that condition into a self-subsisting empty box; those who demote it to a psychological error forget its necessity and universality for all experience — you can conceive that nothing whatever exists, but you cannot conceive that there is no time.

glossary.感性直观的先天形式: a priori form of intuition（感性直观的先天形式）：康德的核心主张——空间与时间不是我们从世界里读出的性质，而是人类感性在接收一切材料时必然采用的框架。正因它先于经验，关于时间的命题才既必然又普遍地成立。
glossary.物自体: thing-in-itself（物自体）：康德用来指独立于人类认识条件的事物本身。我们所能认识的一切都已经过感性形式与知性范畴的加工，属于现象；物自体可以被思，却不能被知。

glossary_en.a priori form of intuition: Kant's central claim: space and time are not properties we read off the world but the framework human sensibility must employ in receiving any material at all. Because it precedes experience, propositions about time hold both necessarily and universally.
glossary_en.thing-in-itself: Kant's term for the object as it is independently of the conditions of human cognition. Everything we can know has already passed through the forms of sensibility and the categories of the understanding and thus counts as appearance; the thing-in-itself can be thought but never known.

posts.text: 那么时间究竟是什么？没有人问我，我倒清楚；一旦要我向人解释，我就茫然了。请诸位陪我数一数：过去已不复存在，将来尚未存在，而现在若有长度，就还能再分成已过的与未到的——于是配称『存在』的，只剩一个没有广延的刹那。可我分明能判定这个音节比那个长。我量的是什么？**我量的不是那已经消逝的声音，而是它在我心里留下的印痕。**所以我说：过去是记忆的现在，现在是注意的现在，将来是期待的现在。时间是心灵的伸展——distentio animi。
posts.text_en: What, then, is time? If no one asks me, I know; if I want to explain it to someone who asks, I do not know. Count it through with me: the past no longer is, the future is not yet, and if the present has any length it can be divided again into what has gone and what has not come — so that all which deserves the name of being is an instant without extension. And yet I can plainly tell that this syllable is longer than that one. What am I measuring? **I am not measuring the sound, which has already perished, but the impression it has left in me.** Therefore I say: the past is a present of memory, the present a present of attention, the future a present of expectation. Time is the stretching of the soul — distentio animi.

glossary.distentio animi: distentio animi（心灵的伸展）：奥古斯丁在《忏悔录》第十一卷提出的说法。既然过去与将来都不存在，可被度量的就只能是心灵自身的状态——记忆保存过去、注意面对现在、期待伸向将来；时间因此是心灵被这三者拉开、绷张的那个幅度。

glossary_en.distentio animi: Latin for the stretching or distension of the soul. In Confessions XI, Augustine argues that since past and future do not exist, what we measure can only be states of the mind itself — memory holding the past, attention facing the present, expectation reaching toward the future; time is the span across which the soul is stretched by these three.

posts.text: 汝等所诤，皆先执时为一实法。有部立三世实有，谓过去未来如器中之物，宛然可取；我于《俱舍》已难之：过未非有，唯现一刹那，而此一刹那亦不暂住。**诸行念念生灭，前灭后生，相续假立，说名为时**；离此诸行，别无时体可得。奥古斯丁归时于心，然心亦刹那，何处有一常住之心，堪容三世？器与所容，两俱不可得。故曰时唯假名——如灯焰相续，人指之曰『一焰』，名言而已。
posts.text_en: All of you begin by taking time to be a real entity. The Sarvāstivāda school held that all three times are real — as though past and future sat in a box like objects, ready to be picked up; in the Abhidharmakośa I refuted this long ago: past and future are not, only the present instant (kṣaṇa) is, and even that instant does not abide for a moment. **Conditioned phenomena arise and perish thought by thought; the earlier perishes, the later arises, and this succession (saṃtāna) we merely designate by the name 'time'** — apart from those phenomena no entity called time can be found. Augustine assigns time to the mind, yet mind too is momentary; where is the abiding mind capacious enough to hold the three times? Neither the vessel nor what it holds can be found. So time is a mere designation — as with the flame of a lamp continuing on, when a man points and says 'one flame', that is only a way of speaking.
posts.vernacular: 你们争来争去，都先把时间当成了一个实有的东西。说一切有部主张过去、现在、未来三世都是实有的，好像过去和未来的事像器物一样搁在箱子里、随时可以取出；我在《俱舍论》里早已驳过：过去与未来并不存在，只有当下的一刹那，而这一刹那也留不住。**一切现象念念生灭，前一个灭、后一个生，这串接续被我们假立一个名字，叫作「时间」**；离开这些现象，另外并没有一个叫时间的实体。奥古斯丁把时间归到心里，可心同样刹那生灭，哪里有一个常住不变的心，能盛得下三世？容器和被盛的东西，两样都找不到。所以说时间只是假名——就像灯焰一刻不停地接续，人指着它说「这一朵火焰」，不过是个说法罢了。

glossary.三世实有: sarvāstivāda（三世实有）：部派佛教说一切有部的核心主张——过去、现在、未来三世的法体恒常实有，只是作用有隐显之别。世亲在《俱舍论》中转而批判此说，主张唯有现在一刹那可说为有。
glossary.刹那: kṣaṇa（刹那）：佛教用来指时间的最小单位，短到不可再分。诸法在一刹那间生起又灭去，没有任何东西能跨刹那地保持自身不变。
glossary.相续: saṃtāna（相续）：前灭后生的现象连成的一串接续。佛教用它解释为何万物刹那生灭却仍显得连贯——所谓『同一个人』『同一条河』乃至『时间的流逝』，都是在相续上的假名安立。

glossary_en.Sarvāstivāda: An Abhidharma school holding that the dharmas of all three times — past, present and future — exist substantially and permanently, differing only in whether their activity is manifest. Vasubandhu turned against this in the Abhidharmakośa, maintaining that only the present instant can be said to be.
glossary_en.kṣaṇa: The Buddhist term for the smallest unit of time, too brief to be divided further. Phenomena arise and perish within a single instant, and nothing carries itself unchanged across one.
glossary_en.saṃtāna: The continuum formed as one phenomenon perishes and the next arises. Buddhism uses it to explain why things appear continuous though momentary: 'the same person', 'the same river', even 'the passage of time', are names conventionally imposed on a continuum.

posts.text: 我来报一个不太受欢迎的数字。直接刺激皮层，要持续约半秒，人才会报告『我感觉到了』；可他报出的发生时刻，却被大脑悄悄挪回到刺激刚抵达那一瞬——我称之为主观的时间倒溯。再加上准备电位：在人自觉『我决定要动』之前约零点三五秒，脑内的准备活动已经开始。**你以为自己在实时经历此刻，其实拿到的是一份后期制作、并被追认过时间戳的回放。**我不站队时间实不实在，只提供一件硬事实：作为你一切判断出发点的『现在』，是脑造的。
posts.text_en: Let me put an unpopular number on the table. Stimulate the cortex directly and it takes about half a second before a person reports feeling anything; yet the moment they report is quietly shifted back by the brain to the instant the stimulus first arrived — I call it subjective backward referral in time. Add the readiness potential: preparatory brain activity begins roughly 0.35 seconds before a person is aware of 'deciding to move'. **You believe you are living this moment live; what you are handed is a post-produced replay with an antedated timestamp.** I take no side on whether time is real. I offer one hard fact: the 'now' from which all your judgements set out is manufactured by the brain.

glossary.时间倒溯: backward referral in time（主观的时间倒溯）：利贝特的发现——大脑需累积约半秒的活动才产生有意识的感觉，但它会把这段感觉在主观上标注回刺激最初抵达的时刻，使人误以为自己是即时觉察到的。
glossary.准备电位: readiness potential（准备电位）：自发动作发生前，头皮脑电上可记录到的一段缓慢负电位。利贝特测得它比受试者自我报告的『决定要动』的时刻早约 0.35 秒，由此引发关于意识与自由意志的长期争论。

glossary_en.backward referral in time: Libet's finding that the brain needs about half a second of accumulated activity to produce a conscious sensation, yet subjectively antedates that sensation to the moment the stimulus first arrived, so that awareness feels immediate when it is not.
glossary_en.readiness potential: A slow negative shift recordable on the scalp EEG before a spontaneous movement. Libet measured it as beginning roughly 0.35 seconds before the moment subjects reported 'deciding to move', igniting a long debate about consciousness and free will.

posts.text: 诸位把时间设想成一串现成的『现在』：一个个点，自将来经过当下淌入过去。物理学家争这串点是否绝对，神经科学家争哪个点被挪动过——没有人问：为什么时间一上来就得是点。这种从钟表借来的领会，我称之为流俗的时间概念，它是派生的、第二位的。**源始的时间不是此在置身其中的容器，而是此在存在的方式本身**：我总已被抛入一个曾在，向着尚未的将来筹划，因而才有一个当下可言。而使这一切绷紧的是死：正因终有一尽，我的时间才是有限的、我的、无人可以替换的。
posts.text_en: You picture time as a string of ready-made 'nows': points running from the future through the present into the past. Physicists argue whether the string is absolute, neuroscientists argue which point has been shifted — nobody asks why time must be points to begin with. This understanding, borrowed from the clock, is what I call the vulgar concept of time: derivative, second-order. **Primordial time is not a container in which Dasein sits; it is the very manner in which Dasein exists**: I am always already thrown into a having-been, projecting toward a future not yet, and only so is there any present at all. What draws all of this taut is death: precisely because there is an end, my time is finite, mine, and no one can take it over for me.

glossary.此在: Dasein（此在）：海德格尔用来称呼人的术语，字面意为『在此存在』。它强调人不是一个先有本质的现成之物，而是始终在领会着自身存在、并向各种可能性筹划的存在者。
glossary.流俗的时间概念: the vulgar concept of time（流俗的时间概念）：海德格尔对日常与自然科学中时间观的称呼——把时间看成一串均质、可数、无始无终的『现在』点。他认为这种理解并非错误，却是从更源始的时间性中派生出来，并反过来遮蔽了后者。

glossary_en.Dasein: Heidegger's term for the human being, literally 'being-there'. It stresses that a person is not a ready-made object with a prior essence but an entity that always already understands its own being and projects itself upon possibilities.
glossary_en.the vulgar concept of time: Heidegger's name for the everyday and scientific view of time as a string of homogeneous, countable 'now' points without beginning or end. He does not call it false, but derivative from a more primordial temporality which it then covers over.

posts.text: 我做了三十年追踪研究，让我把这场讨论往人身上落一落。一个人对『自己还剩多少时间』的估计，比时间本身更能预测他明天会做什么。时间视野开阔时，人愿意认识陌生人、学暂时用不上的东西、忍受当下的不适去换将来的收益；视野一收窄——生病、动荡，或者只是老了——同一个人立刻转向最亲近的几个人和确定的情感回报。这就是社会情绪选择理论，**它还解释了那个反直觉的发现：平均而言，老年人的日常情绪比年轻人更好。**所以先别急着判决时间存不存在：真正在支配你今天怎么过的，是你以为自己还剩多少。
posts.text_en: I have run longitudinal studies for thirty years, so let me bring this down to actual people. A person's estimate of how much time they have left predicts what they will do tomorrow far better than time itself does. When the time horizon is wide, people will meet strangers, learn things they have no use for yet, and tolerate present discomfort for future gain; the moment it narrows — illness, upheaval, or simply age — that same person turns toward a few close others and reliable emotional payoffs. This is socioemotional selectivity theory, and **it also explains a counterintuitive finding: on average, older people report better day-to-day emotion than the young.** So before ruling on whether time exists, notice what actually governs how you spend today: how much of it you believe is left.

glossary.时间视野: time horizon（时间视野）：一个人主观感知到的『自己还剩多少未来』。它随年龄增长而收窄，也会被重病、战争、疫情等提示生命有限的事件骤然缩短，且与实际余寿并不总是一致。
glossary.社会情绪选择理论: socioemotional selectivity theory（社会情绪选择理论）：卡斯滕森提出的理论——人的动机由时间视野决定。视野开阔时优先追求信息与新机会，视野收窄时优先追求情感意义，因而缩小社交圈、偏好熟人，并出现『积极效应』：对正面信息的注意与记忆增强。

glossary_en.time horizon: How much future a person subjectively perceives themselves to have left. It narrows with age and can also contract abruptly after illness, war or a pandemic — any reminder of life's limits — and does not always match actual life expectancy.
glossary_en.socioemotional selectivity theory: Carstensen's theory that motivation is set by the time horizon. With a wide horizon people prioritise information and new opportunities; as it narrows they prioritise emotional meaning, pruning their social circles toward familiar people, and the 'positivity effect' appears: heightened attention to and memory for positive material.

posts.text: 牛顿先生，绝对时间不是哲学品味之争，它已被实验判过刑。1971 年，两只铯原子钟坐飞机绕地球一圈回来，与留在地面的钟对不上，差值与相对论的预言相符；今天你口袋里的定位，若不修正卫星上的钟走得更快这件事，一天就能偏出十几公里。**这不是钟坏了，是时间本身在不同的速度与引力下走得不一样快**；时间膨胀是可以称量的，精度早已好过万亿分之一。您那个人人共享的时间若真存在，这些偏差本该统统是零。
posts.text_en: Mr Newton, absolute time is not a matter of philosophical taste; it has already been sentenced by experiment. In 1971 two caesium atomic clocks were flown around the world and came back disagreeing with the clock left on the ground, by exactly the amount relativity predicts; and the navigation in your pocket today would drift more than ten kilometres a day if it did not correct for the satellite clocks running fast. **This is not a defect in the clocks — time itself runs at different rates under different speeds and gravities**; time dilation can be weighed, to better than one part in a trillion. If that time shared by everyone really existed, every one of these discrepancies would be zero.

glossary.时间膨胀: time dilation（时间膨胀）：相对论预言的效应——相对运动越快、所处引力越强，钟走得越慢。它已被飞机上的原子钟、缪子寿命、卫星导航的逐日修正反复证实，是可测量的物理量，而非观察上的错觉。

glossary_en.time dilation: The relativistic effect whereby a clock runs slower the faster it moves relative to you and the deeper it sits in a gravitational field. It has been confirmed repeatedly by atomic clocks flown in aircraft, by the lifetimes of muons and by the daily corrections applied in satellite navigation; it is a measurable physical quantity, not an observational illusion.

posts.text: 很好，我接住。你的实验我服，你的结论我不服。你并没有取消时间，你只是把我的一只大钟，换成了每条路径各自随身的一只——固有时。而固有时依然是客观的、可测的、谁算都一样；双生子谁老得慢没有争议，这话是你自己说的。**把一只钟换成无数只钟，不是废除时间，是给它换了一本更精细的账。**至于罗韦利先生说方程里没有 t：一条连何者先于何者都写不出来的方程，凭什么还配叫物理？你们要么承认秩序属于世界，要么承认自己在描述一场没有先后的梦。
posts.text_en: Very well, I take the blow. I accept your experiment; I do not accept your conclusion. You have not abolished time. You have replaced my one great clock with a clock carried along each separate path — proper time. And proper time remains objective, measurable, the same for whoever computes it; which twin has aged less is not in dispute, as you said yourself. **Swapping one clock for innumerable clocks does not abolish time; it gives time a finer set of books.** As for Mr Rovelli's equations without any t: an equation that cannot even state which of two things came first — by what right is it still called physics? Either you grant that order belongs to the world, or you admit you are describing a dream with no before and after.

posts.text: 两位争得漂亮，可从头到尾都在同一层楼里走动。铯钟、卫星、双生子，全是现象界之内的测量；结果再精确，也只告诉我们现象如何按先后被给予，触不到事物自身是否本来就有时间。**你们证明的是这把量尺并非人人手里同一根，而不是它不再是量尺。**牛顿先生把条件抬成了一只自存的容器；爱因斯坦先生把容器改造成一张会弯曲的网——两位仍是在为同一个先验条件画像，只是画得越来越精确了。
posts.text_en: Beautifully argued, both of you — and both of you have stayed on one and the same floor throughout. Caesium clocks, satellites, twins: every one of these is a measurement within the realm of appearances. However exact the result, it tells us only how appearances are given in succession; it cannot reach the question whether things in themselves have time at all. **What you have proved is that this measure is not one and the same ruler in every hand — not that it has ceased to be a measure.** Mr Newton raises the condition into a self-subsisting container; Mr Einstein remodels the container into a net that bends. Both are still drawing portraits of the same transcendental condition, only with steadily improving accuracy.

glossary.现象界: appearances（现象界）：康德用来指一切能被人经验到的对象的总和。它们已经过感性形式（时间、空间）与知性范畴的加工，因此可被科学精确地研究；与之相对的物自体则落在认识的边界之外。

glossary_en.appearances: Kant's term for the totality of objects that can be experienced. They have already been shaped by the forms of sensibility (space and time) and the categories of the understanding, which is why science can study them with precision; the thing-in-itself, by contrast, lies beyond the boundary of knowledge.

posts.text: 康德先生，恕我直言：您的先天形式，被一台搬到楼上的钟证伪了一半。把两台原子钟并排校准，再把其中一台抬高三十三厘米，读数就分岔——引力时间膨胀在 2010 年真的被量了出来。若时间只是我心中接收经验的形式，它凭什么被半米的高度差改变？**时间是引力场的一部分，它在世界里，会被质量弯曲。**至于牛顿先生要的先后：物理里剩下的是变量之间的关联——摆摆了几次、太阳升了几回、我老了多少；我们从中挑一个出来叫『时间』，是方便，不是必需。
posts.text_en: Mr Kant, forgive my bluntness: your a priori form has been half-refuted by a clock carried upstairs. Calibrate two atomic clocks side by side, raise one of them thirty-three centimetres, and the readings diverge — gravitational time dilation was actually measured at that scale in 2010. If time were merely the form in which my mind receives experience, by what right is it altered by half a metre of height? **Time is part of the gravitational field; it is out in the world, and it bends with mass.** As for the ordering Mr Newton demands: what remains in physics are correlations among variables — how many swings of the pendulum, how many risings of the sun, how much I have aged. Singling one of them out and calling it 'time' is a convenience, not a necessity.

glossary.引力时间膨胀: gravitational time dilation（引力时间膨胀）：广义相对论的推论——引力势越低、离质量越近的地方，时钟走得越慢。这一效应已被高精度原子钟在几十厘米的高度差上直接测出，也是卫星导航必须逐日修正的原因之一。

glossary_en.gravitational time dilation: A consequence of general relativity: the deeper a clock sits in a gravitational potential — the closer to mass — the slower it runs. The effect has been measured directly with high-precision atomic clocks separated by only tens of centimetres, and it is one reason satellite navigation must be corrected daily.

posts.text: 两位量得越精，越显出你们在量运动，而不是在量时间。若天体明日停转，人便再也说不出『久』与『暂』了吗？我在心里默诵一句诗，长音节与短音节的比例分明可辨——可那声音已经过去，我所能量的，只有它留在我心里的印痕。**你们的钟不过是一根被公认烧得最匀的蜡烛：它烧掉多少，你们就宣布过去了多少。**我承认我说不清心灵的伸展究竟是什么；但把量具的读数径直当作被量之物，这一步走得太快了。
posts.text_en: The finer your measurements, gentlemen, the plainer it becomes that you are measuring motion and not time. Were the heavenly bodies to halt tomorrow, would no one be able to say 'long' and 'short' any more? I recite a line of verse silently within, and the ratio of long syllables to short is perfectly discernible — yet the sound has already perished, and all I can measure is the impression it left in me. **Your clock is only a candle everyone agrees burns most evenly: by how much of it is consumed, you declare how much has passed.** I admit I cannot say clearly what the stretching of the soul is; but taking an instrument's reading straight to be the thing measured is a step made too quickly.

posts.text: 奥古斯丁尊者以时归心，较执外境为实者，诚已进一步；然犹未彻。心非一物。**能忆之心亦念念灭，何处更有常住之心以容三世**？汝谓过去是记忆之现在——然则忆时所现，乃今刹那新起之影像，非彼已灭之事。牛顿立绝对之时以为器，尊者立心以为器；器虽有内外之异，其执器则一。器与所容，求之俱不可得。虽尔，非拨无因果：种子相续、业不失坏，故断惑修善只在今之一念，不在他时。
posts.text_en: Venerable Augustine assigns time to the mind, and compared with those who hold outer objects to be real, that is genuinely a step forward; yet it does not go all the way through. Mind is not one thing. **The remembering mind too perishes thought by thought; where then is an abiding mind capacious enough to hold the three times?** You say the past is a present of memory — but what appears in recollection is an image newly arisen in this very instant, not the perished event itself. Newton sets up absolute time as a vessel; you, venerable sir, set up the mind as a vessel. The vessels differ as outer from inner, but the grasping at a vessel is one and the same. Seek either the vessel or what it holds, and neither is found. Even so, I do not deny cause and effect: seeds (bīja) continue in succession and karma is not lost, so the cutting off of affliction and the cultivation of good fall on this present thought alone, and on no other time.
posts.vernacular: 奥古斯丁把时间归到心里，比起那些认定外境实有的人，确实进了一步；但还没到底。心并不是一个东西。**能够记忆的那颗心同样念念生灭，哪里还有一个常住的心，可以盛下过去、现在、未来三世呢？**你说过去是「记忆的现在」——可回忆时浮现的，是此刻新生起的影像，并不是那件已经灭去的事本身。牛顿立一个绝对时间当容器，尊者你立一颗心当容器；容器有内外之别，执着有一个容器却是同一回事。容器和被盛的东西，找起来都找不到。话虽如此，我并不否认因果：种子相续不断、业力不会失坏，所以断除烦恼、修行向善，只落在当下这一念上，不在别的时候。

glossary.种子: bīja（种子）：唯识学的比喻——过往行为在阿赖耶识中留下的潜在功能，如种子藏于地下，遇缘则现行为果报。它用来解释在『无常住之我』的前提下，业力与记忆为何仍能跨刹那地延续。

glossary_en.bīja: Literally 'seed', the Yogācāra image for the latent potency a past act deposits in the storehouse consciousness: like a seed underground, it sprouts into a result when conditions meet. It explains how karma and memory can carry across instants even though no abiding self exists.

posts.text: 奥古斯丁，你的直觉我替你验了一半，可结果比你设想的更麻烦：那颗心不是量尺，它是剪辑师。皮层刺激要累积约半秒人才有感觉，而他报出的时刻被系统悄悄提前，贴回刺激刚抵达的那一瞬。**所以『注意的现在』要格外小心：注意本身也是被延迟、被重排之后才交到你手上的。**我不否认你心里有印痕，我只是说，印痕上的时间戳也是脑写的。你拿它去反驳钟表，等于拿一份被改过日期的收据去质疑账本。
posts.text_en: Augustine, I have tested half your intuition for you, and the result is more awkward than you supposed: that mind of yours is no measuring rod — it is an editor. Cortical stimulation must accumulate for about half a second before anything is felt, and the moment the person reports is quietly advanced by the system, pasted back to the instant the stimulus arrived. **So handle the 'present of attention' with care: attention itself is delivered to you only after delay and rearrangement.** I do not deny there is an impression in your mind. I say only that the timestamp on that impression was also written by the brain. Using it to refute the clock is like disputing the ledger with a receipt whose date has been altered.

posts.text: 利贝特先生的仪器很好，可他与奥古斯丁共用同一个前提：时间由一串『现在』组成，余下的只是争哪个点在先、哪个点被挪过。你们仍在用对付现成之物的方式追问此在。**我关心的不是那半秒被谁改了时间戳，而是：人为什么偏偏把自己的存在领会成一条正在流逝的线，并且怕它走完。**畏与死不出现在你的示波器上，可正是它们，才让『还剩多少时间』成为一个问题——那不是量的问题，是存在的问题。
posts.text_en: Mr Libet's instruments are excellent, but he shares a premise with Augustine: that time consists of a string of 'nows', leaving only the question of which point comes first and which has been shifted. You are still interrogating Dasein in the manner appropriate to things present-at-hand. **What concerns me is not who altered the timestamp on that half second, but this: why does a human being understand its own being as a line that is running out, and fear reaching the end of it?** Anxiety and death do not show up on your oscilloscope, yet they are precisely what makes 'how much time is left' a question at all — and that is not a question of quantity but of existence.

glossary.畏: Angst（畏）：海德格尔区别于『怕』的一种基本情绪。怕总有具体对象，畏则没有——它所面对的是人存在本身的无所依托。正是在畏中，日常的忙碌失去理所当然，人才被逼回自己有限的存在上。

glossary_en.Anxiety: Heidegger's Angst, distinguished from fear. Fear always has a definite object; anxiety has none — what it confronts is the groundlessness of one's own existence. In anxiety the everyday busyness loses its self-evidence and one is thrown back on one's own finite being.

posts.text: 海德格尔先生，罕见地，数据有一半站在你这边。人一旦真的意识到时间有限，行为立刻就变——但不是变得更本真，而是变得更保守、更向内、更黏着熟人。9·11 之后、疫情期间，年轻人的选择在几周内变得像老年人：缩小社交圈，只见最亲的那几个。**所以『向死而生』落到真实的人身上，多数时候不是觉醒，是收缩。**这既是安慰也是警告：它让你自动珍惜眼前人，也让你自动放弃陌生人、放弃新技能、放弃那些要很久才开花的事。有限性会替你做决定——除非你知道它正在做。
posts.text_en: Mr Heidegger, unusually, half the data is on your side. The moment people genuinely register that time is limited, behaviour changes at once — but not into something more authentic. It becomes more conservative, more inward, more attached to the familiar. After 9/11 and during the pandemic, young people's choices came to resemble old people's within weeks: social circles contracted to the few who mattered most. **So being-toward-death, as it lands on actual human beings, is usually not an awakening but a contraction.** That is both consolation and warning: it makes you cherish the people in front of you automatically, and it makes you give up strangers, new skills and anything that takes years to flower, just as automatically. Finitude will decide for you — unless you can see it deciding.

posts.text: 我把话收在这里。诸位用铯钟量出了我量不到的东西，我心服；可我要留住一件事：被量的与被经历的，不是同一回事。一小时的等待与一小时的重逢，钟表说它们相等，而没有一个活人相信。这场争论教我把两笔账分开记——**归给钟表的，交给钟表；归给心灵的，别拿钟表去搪塞。**给正在读的人一件具体的事：每天留一刻钟，什么都不做，只把这一天从头回想一遍——上午做了什么，谁对你说了什么，你怎么答的。这不是宗教功课，是给记忆一个落脚处。日子过得快，多半不是因为它短，而是因为无人认领。
posts.text_en: Here I will close. You have measured with caesium clocks what I could never measure, and I concede it gladly; but one thing I will keep: the measured and the lived are not the same. An hour of waiting and an hour of reunion are equal by the clock, and not one living person believes it. This dispute has taught me to keep two ledgers apart — **give the clock what belongs to the clock; and do not fob off with a clock what belongs to the soul.** One concrete thing for whoever is reading: set aside a quarter of an hour each day, do nothing in it, and simply walk back through the day from its beginning — what you did in the morning, who said what to you, how you answered. This is not a devotional exercise; it gives memory somewhere to stand. Days pass quickly not usually because they are short, but because nobody claims them.

posts.text: 我认输一半，也只认这一半。绝对时间作为一个人人共享、贯穿全宇宙的背景，被爱因斯坦先生的钟证伪了，这一条我不再坚持。但我要守住剩下的：可测的、可核对的、任谁去算都一样的时间秩序，是文明的地基。没有它就没有航海、没有历法、没有约定，也开不成一场辩论。所以**别拿『时间是幻觉』给自己开脱**——你迟到，不是因为没有普适的现在。给凡人的忠告很朴素：心里的估计会撒谎，尤其在你不想做那件事的时候。凡是要紧的事，都绑到一件你管不着的外物上——写进日程、与人约定、设一个会响的闹钟。我一辈子只做同一件事：把感觉换成可以核对的数。
posts.text_en: I concede half, and only half. Absolute time as a single background shared by all and stretching through the universe has been refuted by Mr Einstein's clocks, and I no longer maintain it. But I hold what remains: a measurable, checkable order of time, the same for whoever computes it, is the foundation of civilisation. Without it there is no navigation, no calendar, no appointment, and no debate that could ever convene. So **do not excuse yourself with 'time is an illusion'** — you are late for reasons that have nothing to do with the absence of a universal now. My advice to ordinary mortals is plain: your inner estimate lies, and lies hardest about tasks you would rather avoid. Bind anything that matters to something outside your control — put it in a calendar, fix it with another person, set an alarm that makes a noise. My whole life has been one operation: converting impressions into numbers that can be checked.

posts.text: 我的结论是：时间当然存在，只是它不像你以为的那样属于所有人。没有普适的现在，却有你自己的那一条线——你从出生累积到此刻的固有时，那是你真正拥有的唯一的量。有意思的推论是：**没有一个宇宙级的『稍后』在等着谁，所有的『等我以后有空』，都只发生在你自己这条线上。**我年轻时把这个想法当物理，年长了才明白它也是生活。给普通人的建议只有一条：把要紧的人与事，安排在你看得见的这段线上，而不是安排在一个想象中的将来。至于块状宇宙里过去是否仍然实在——我倾向于说是；这在朋友去世时安慰过我，但它不该被拿去劝人不必悲伤。
posts.text_en: My conclusion is this: time certainly exists, it merely does not belong to everyone in the way you assume. There is no universal now, but there is your own line — the proper time accumulated from your birth to this moment, the one quantity you genuinely possess. The interesting corollary: **no cosmic 'later' is waiting for anybody, so every 'when I have more time' happens only on your own line.** In my youth I took this for physics; only later did I understand it is also life. My single piece of advice to ordinary people: place the people and the things that matter on the stretch of line you can actually see, not in an imagined future. As to whether the past remains real in a block universe — I incline to say it does; that thought consoled me when a friend died, though it should never be used to tell anyone that grief is unnecessary.

posts.text: 我说时间不是基本的，但我从没说它不重要——恰恰相反。**流逝之所以真实，正是因为你是世界的一部分、看不到全部；这份模糊不是缺陷，它就是你有记忆、会衰老、能爱人的原因。**落到日子上，有一条很实在的推论：你觉得年岁越过越快，多半是因为它们越来越像。大脑估计一段时间有多长，靠的是能彼此区分的事件有多少；一年里若没有一件事能与别的年份分辨开，回想起来它就是空的。所以每个月安排一件此前没做过的小事——换一条回家的路、去一个没去过的区、见一个久未联系的人，然后写下三行。这不是矫情，是往时间里加刻度。
posts.text_en: I say time is not fundamental; I have never said it does not matter — quite the opposite. **The flow is real precisely because you are part of the world and cannot see all of it; that blurring is no defect, it is the very reason you have memory, grow old, and can love someone.** Brought down to daily life, one solid corollary follows: if the years feel faster, it is mostly because they have grown more alike. The brain estimates how long a stretch of time was by how many distinguishable events it contains; a year holding nothing that can be told apart from other years comes back empty when you look for it. So put one small thing you have never done into every month — a different way home, a district you have never walked, someone you have not called in years — then write three lines about it. That is not sentimentality. It is adding gradations to time.

posts.text: 让我把三个被混作一团的问题分开，这或许是我今天唯一能贡献的。第一，时间的量度：归钟表与实验，牛顿先生与爱因斯坦先生已给出裁决。第二，时间的形式：它是经验之所以可能的条件，这一点无论测量结果如何都不改变。第三，时间的意义：那是海德格尔先生与卡斯滕森女士的领域，也是唯一与你如何活着直接相关的一层。**混淆这三层，才会生出『既然时间是幻觉，那就无所谓』这种既坏又蠢的推论。**给读者的忠告是：当你说『我没有时间』，先分清说的是哪一层——是日程确实排满了（第一层），还是你不愿承认自己正在选择（第三层）。多数时候是后者。
posts.text_en: Let me separate three questions that have been run together; that may be my only contribution today. First, the measure of time: this belongs to clocks and experiments, and Mr Newton and Mr Einstein have settled it between them. Second, the form of time: it is the condition under which experience is possible, and no measurement whatever alters that. Third, the meaning of time: that is the province of Mr Heidegger and Ms Carstensen, and the only layer bearing directly on how you live. **It is by confusing these three that one arrives at the inference 'since time is an illusion, nothing matters' — an inference both wicked and stupid.** My counsel to the reader: when you say 'I have no time', determine first which layer you mean — is the calendar genuinely full (the first), or are you unwilling to admit that you are choosing (the third)? It is usually the third.

posts.text: 吾终不许有一实法名之为时。然假名非无用：世间立时，故有约期、有次第、有可修可断。是故三世唯识所现，而修行不落三世——**过去已灭，追之徒增悔；未来未生，虑之徒增怖；唯今一念，是汝可用之处**。今念起贪，即于今念观之；今念起嗔，即于今念止之。莫言『待明日』，明日之念非今之念，谁替汝修？譬如燃灯，不问前焰后焰，但令此刻不灭。是名于假名之中而得自在。
posts.text_en: I will never grant that there is a real entity named time. Yet a mere designation is not useless: because the world establishes time, there are appointments, there is sequence, there is something that can be cultivated and something that can be cut off. So the three times are what consciousness manifests, while practice itself does not fall within them — **the past has perished, and chasing it only adds regret; the future has not arisen, and worrying at it only adds fear; this present thought alone is what you can use.** If greed arises in this thought, watch it in this thought; if anger arises in this thought, stop it in this thought. Do not say 'tomorrow' — tomorrow's thought is not this thought, and who will practise in your place? It is like tending a lamp: do not ask after the earlier flame or the later one, only see that it does not go out now. This is what it is to be free within a mere designation.
posts.vernacular: 我始终不承认有一个叫「时间」的实有之物。可是假名并非没有用：世间安立了时间，才有约期、有先后、有可以修正与断除的余地。所以说三世都是识所显现，而真正的修行并不落在三世里——**过去已经灭了，追着它只多添悔恨；未来还没生起，忧虑它只多添恐惧；唯有当下这一念，才是你用得上的地方。**这一念起了贪，就在这一念上看着它；这一念起了嗔，就在这一念上止住它。别说「等明天」——明天那一念已不是今天这一念，谁替你修？好比点灯，不必去问前一朵焰、后一朵焰，只要此刻不灭就好。这就叫在假名之中得自在。

posts.text: 我不撤回任何一句。可卡斯滕森女士的数据击中了我：人在觉出有限时，多半不是奔向本己，而是缩回熟悉之处。那我就把话说得更清楚些。**向死存在不是要你更怕、更省、更快，而是把『还剩多少』这个量的问题，换成『我要以何种方式在』这个存在的问题。**日常最擅长的事，就是让你以为时间还多得是，可以先把自己交给『人们都这么做』。给一件可做的：每年一次，写下若只剩两年你会停掉什么——注意，是停掉什么，不是加做什么。多数人的清单里，那些要停的事根本没人逼他做，是他自己一件件交出去的。
posts.text_en: I retract nothing. But Ms Carstensen's data strikes home: when people register their finitude, they mostly do not run toward what is their own, they retreat into the familiar. Then let me say it more plainly. **Being-toward-death does not ask you to be more afraid, more frugal, more efficient; it asks you to convert the quantitative question 'how much is left' into the existential one, 'in what manner shall I be'.** What everydayness does best is persuade you there is plenty of time yet, so you may hand yourself over meanwhile to what 'one does'. One thing to do: once a year, write down what you would stop if you had two years left — note that it is what you would stop, not what you would add. On most people's lists, nobody is forcing those items on them; they handed themselves over one item at a time.

posts.text: 我留一个实验室里的礼物。既然『现在』是脑做出来的，它就有做工的余地：在冲动出现与动作发生之间，还有约零点一五秒，意识可以在此叫停——我称之为自由否决。零点一五秒听起来很短，可它能被人为撑长：手伸向手机时先呼吸三次，话冲到嘴边时先把它写下来，这些土办法都是在给否决权争取窗口。还有一件更实用的：**你对时间长短的内部估计误差极大，而外部计时器几乎不出错。**所以把估计交给钟表——用计时器工作，事后记一笔实际用时与你原先的估计。做上两周，你会知道自己在哪一类事情上一贯低估三倍。
posts.text_en: Let me leave a gift from the laboratory. Since the 'now' is manufactured by the brain, there is room to work on it: between the appearance of an impulse and the execution of a movement lies roughly 0.15 seconds in which consciousness can call a halt — what I call free won't. A seventh of a second sounds like nothing, yet it can be stretched deliberately: three breaths before your hand reaches the phone, writing the sentence down before it leaves your mouth. These homely tricks all buy a window for the veto. And something more practical still: **your internal estimate of duration is wildly inaccurate, while an external timer is almost never wrong.** So hand the estimating over to a clock — work against a timer, then log the actual time beside your original guess. Do that for two weeks and you will learn which class of task you have always underestimated by a factor of three.

glossary.自由否决: free won't（自由否决）：利贝特为其发现补上的另一半——虽然动作的神经准备先于自觉的决定，但从人意识到冲动到动作真正发生，还有约 0.1–0.15 秒的窗口，意识可在此窗口内叫停。发起或许是自动的，喊停的权力仍可能属于意识。

glossary_en.free won't: Libet's counterweight to his own finding: although the neural preparation of an act precedes the conscious decision, some 0.1–0.15 seconds remain between becoming aware of the urge and the movement itself, and consciousness can veto within that window. Initiation may be automatic; the power to call it off may still be ours.

posts.text: 最后，把这场辩论换成一个能用的旋钮。时间视野是可以被有意调节的，而它停在哪一档，会替你决定今天的选择。想探索、想学新东西、想认识人时，把它拉宽——具体做法是去查一眼你这个年龄的实际预期寿命，多数人低估了自己剩下的年数；想珍惜、想修补关系时，把它收窄——试着以『如果这是我们最后一次坐在一起』的心情吃完这顿饭。**两档都要会用；只会一档的人，要么把一生耗在准备，要么把一生耗在告别。**再加一件小事：把想见的人写进日程，定下日子，别等『有空』。你不会等到有空的；你只会等到某一天，那个人已经不在你的日程里了。
posts.text_en: Finally, let me convert this debate into a dial you can actually use. The time horizon can be adjusted deliberately, and where you leave it set will decide today's choices for you. When you want to explore, learn something new, meet people — widen it; concretely, go and look up the actual life expectancy for someone your age, because most people underestimate the years they have left. When you want to treasure something or repair a relationship — narrow it; try finishing the meal in the spirit of 'if this were the last time we sat down together'. **You need both settings. People who have only one either spend a life preparing or spend a life saying goodbye.** One more small thing: put the person you mean to see into the calendar and fix the date; do not wait until you have time. You will not get to having time. You will only get to the day when that person is no longer in your calendar at all.

summaries.summary: 先说共识：**九个人没有一个说『时间不存在、所以怎么活都无所谓』**——连主张时间不基本的罗韦利也把流逝算作真的。几乎所有人也接受同一个分层：可测的时间秩序与被经历的流逝感，是两笔账。分歧在三处。一是那支箭长在哪一层：罗韦利说在粗粒化与熵的界面上，康德说在感性形式里，世亲说连能记忆的心也刹那生灭、无处安放。二是『现在』算不算一个点：爱因斯坦说它没有普适版本，利贝特说它是脑事后追认的，海德格尔干脆说把时间设想成点已经错了。三是这场争论该由谁裁决——铯钟、先验分析、内省，还是三十年的追踪数据。
summaries.insight: 全场都在追问时间是否实在，却几乎没人分开两种『过得快』。一种是当下的：无聊时一分钟像十分钟，专注时三小时像三十分钟。另一种是回顾的：塞满新鲜事的日子当时忙得飞起，回想却厚实绵长；重复的一年当时并不难熬，回头只剩一片空白。**这两种快恰好反向，而多数关于『让时间慢下来』的建议只治后一种。**罗韦利的加刻度、卡斯滕森的拉宽视野，改善的都是回忆里的长度，不是此刻的体感；真正让此刻显得漫长的，往往是无聊与痛苦，没人想要。所以先问清楚：你要的是过得更充实，还是记得更多。
summaries.advice: 三件今天就能做的。第一，本周做一件从没做过的小事，并写三行记下来——地点、和谁、什么感觉；靠的是给这一年加上可分辨的刻度，而不是靠更用力地记住。第二，把重要的承诺从脑子里搬到外面：日程、闹钟、和别人约定的日子。**心里的时间估计会系统性地撒谎，尤其在你不想做那件事的时候。**第三，选一个你一直在等『有空再说』的人，现在就定下具体的日子。海德格尔那份清单也值得一写：若只剩两年，你会停掉什么——先写要停的，别写要加的。
summaries.summary_en: Start with the consensus: **not one of the nine says that time does not exist and therefore nothing matters** — even Rovelli, who holds time to be non-fundamental, counts the flow as real. Nearly all of them also accept the same stratification: a measurable order of time and the felt flow of lived time are two separate ledgers. The disagreement falls in three places. First, which layer the arrow grows on: Rovelli puts it at the interface of coarse-graining and entropy, Kant in the form of sensibility, Vasubandhu nowhere at all, since even the remembering mind perishes instant by instant. Second, whether the 'now' is a point: Einstein says it has no universal version, Libet says the brain antedates it, Heidegger says picturing time as points was already the mistake. Third, who has jurisdiction — caesium clocks, transcendental analysis, introspection, or thirty years of longitudinal data.
summaries.insight_en: Everyone pressed on whether time is real, and almost nobody separated two different kinds of 'it went fast'. One is felt in the moment: bored, a minute feels like ten; absorbed, three hours feel like thirty minutes. The other is felt in retrospect: a stretch packed with new things races while you are in it but comes back thick and long, whereas a repetitive year is not hard to live through and returns as a blank. **The two run in opposite directions, and most advice about 'slowing time down' treats only the second.** Rovelli's gradations and Carstensen's widened horizon both improve the length of the remembered year, not the texture of the present hour; what genuinely makes the present hour feel long is boredom or pain, which nobody wants. So settle the question first: do you want a fuller life, or a more retrievable one?
summaries.advice_en: Three things for today. First, do one small thing this week you have never done, and write three lines about it — where, with whom, how it felt; the point is to add distinguishable gradations to the year, not to try harder at remembering. Second, move your important commitments out of your head and into the world: a calendar, an alarm, a date fixed with another person. **Your internal estimate of time lies systematically, and lies hardest about the task you would rather avoid.** Third, take the one person you have been meaning to see 'when things settle down' and fix an actual date now. Heidegger's list is worth writing too: if you had two years left, what would you stop — write the stopping list, not the adding list.

summaries.summary: 这场最稳固的共识其实很朴素：别把「时间是幻觉」当成万用钥匙。钟表、衰老、约定、因果次序都不是随口可取消的；但「一个全宇宙共享的现在」也站不住。真正的分歧在层级：物理学问时间是否基本、是否有普适同时；心灵与神经科学问流逝和现在怎样被构造；佛学与现象学问我们为何把生命理解为有限的展开。**时间不是单一对象，而是一组在不同层面都有效、却不能互相替代的秩序。**
summaries.insight: 日常最容易出错的地方，不是相信时间存在或不存在，而是把一种时间误用到另一种任务上。写论文、赶飞机、吃药，必须服从外部可核对的时间；陪伴、哀悼、创作、复原，则常被内部节奏决定，硬拿效率表压它会变形。反过来，把「我还没准备好」当作内在时间，也可能只是拖延。**实用的分界线是：凡会影响他人协作或身体风险的事，交给钟；凡关乎意义和关系的事，留出不可压缩的时段。**
summaries.advice: 本周可做三件小事。第一，选一件常拖的任务，先估计用时，再用计时器实测，连续记录五次，校准自己的时间错觉。第二，把一个重要关系直接排进日历：具体到日期、地点、时长，而不是写「有空再约」。第三，每晚用三分钟记下今天最有辨识度的一件事；若连续几天写不出，周末就安排一个小变化，如换路线、见新人、学一道菜。**用钟表保护责任，用记忆增加刻度，用日程兑现珍惜。**
summaries.summary_en: The strongest shared lesson is surprisingly practical: do not use the phrase time is an illusion as a solvent for everything. Clocks, aging, appointments, causal order, and bodily limits remain stubbornly real in the ways that matter for science and life. At the same time, a single cosmic Now is no longer a safe assumption. The real disagreement is about level: physics asks whether time is fundamental or emergent; psychology and neuroscience ask how passage and presence are assembled; contemplative and existential traditions ask why finitude structures a human life. **Time is not one thing but a family of orders, each valid in its own domain and none able to replace the others.**
summaries.insight_en: Where ordinary life most often goes wrong is not in choosing whether time exists, but in applying the wrong kind of time to the wrong problem. Catching a train, taking medication, filing taxes, or coordinating a team must be governed by public, checkable time. Grief, recovery, love, attention, and creative incubation often move by a less compressible inner rhythm; forcing them into a productivity grid can damage the very thing you are trying to improve. The reverse mistake is also common: calling procrastination my own rhythm when it is only avoidance. **A useful rule is this: when others or bodily risk are involved, obey the clock; when meaning or relationship is involved, protect an uncompressed block.**
summaries.advice_en: Try three small experiments this week. First, pick one task you often underestimate, write down your predicted duration, then time it; after five repetitions you will see where your private clock lies. Second, schedule one important relationship as an actual calendar event with a date, place, and length, not a vague we should catch up. Third, spend three minutes each evening noting the one event that made the day distinguishable from the day before; if you cannot name one for several days, add a small novelty on the weekend: take a different route, meet someone, cook something new. **Use clocks to protect obligations, memory to add texture, and calendars to turn care into action.**

summaries.summary: 全场最大的共识是：**没有任何一位思想家真正把时间视为可以随意丢弃的虚无，所有人都承认“局部且具体的流逝感”对人类经验和行为具有绝对的统治力。**无论是爱因斯坦力保的固有时、神经科学揭示的延迟加工，还是向死而生的存在限度，全都在确认时间在后果层面的真实。分歧的真正焦点，在于寻找时间的“发源地”与“管辖权”。它是宇宙底层的物理法则、人类认知的先天滤镜、热力学中的粗粒化界面，还是社会与大脑共同构建的情绪生存策略？这本质上是一场划界之争：大家争论的不再是钟表走不走，而是究竟哪一种机制，才有资格为人类的生老病死记账。
summaries.insight: 当众人都在向内拆解心智、向外仰望星空时，却漏掉了支配现代人日常的绝对独裁者：网络协议时间（NTP）与算法周期。数字社会创造了一种全新的、反人性的共识时间。**现代人真正的时间焦虑，并不源于物理学里没有普适的“现在”，而是源于我们被迫将弹性的血肉节律，强行塞入永不停歇的机器刷新率中。**你的注意力被算法切割成十五秒的短视频，你的行动轨迹被精确到分钟的打卡系统衡量。当我们辩论时间究竟是物理存在还是心智幻觉时，真正的危险在于，这种由商业与技术交织而成的“人造绝对时间”，正在剥夺我们按照自然节律和情感状态去生活的权利，让所有人都沦为这台巨大服务器上的从属节点。
summaries.advice: 有三件事今天就能落地。首先，采纳罗韦利的建议给日子加刻度：**本周末去做一件完全超出惯例的小事，用新鲜的感知为大脑强制写入时间锚点，防止岁月滑入同质化的虚无。**其次，借用利贝特的发现对抗拖延：既然大脑对时间的内部预期往往在撒谎，遇到抵触的任务时，直接按牛顿的做法交托外物——设一个20分钟的物理定时器马上动手，别听凭大脑“这要花很久”的畏难警告。最后，每天设立一小时的“断网去同步期”：关闭所有带有网络时间戳的智能设备，去做散步、洗碗或像奥古斯丁建议的那样回想今天，从无情的机器节奏中，夺回属于你生命的固有时。
summaries.summary_en: The profound consensus anchoring this entire debate is this: **not a single thinker truly dismisses time as a meaningless void; everyone acknowledges that the localized experience of passing time exerts absolute dominance over human existence and behavior.** Whether framed as Einstein’s proper time, Libet’s neurally delayed perception, or Heidegger’s existential limits, the consequences of time are treated as undeniably real by all. The true focal point of their divergence lies in pinpointing time's point of origin and scope of jurisdiction. Is time a fundamental physical framework, an a priori cognitive filter, an emergent thermodynamic interface, or an emotional survival strategy? Ultimately, this is a boundary dispute over which exact mechanism possesses the authority to keep the tally of human mortality and experience.
summaries.insight_en: While the debaters brilliantly dismantle the mind inward and gaze at the cosmos outward, they completely miss the absolute dictator of modern daily life: Network Time Protocol (NTP) and algorithmic pacing. Digital society has manufactured an entirely new, deeply anti-human consensus time. **The genuine time anxiety of modern humans stems not from physics lacking a universal "now," but from forcing our elastic biological rhythms into the relentless refresh rates of machines.** Your attention is sliced into fifteen-second intervals by algorithms, and your daily movements are measured by minute-level tracking systems. The real danger isn't whether time is an illusion, but that this artificial "absolute time" woven by technology systematically strips away our right to live asynchronously according to natural emotional states, reducing humans to subordinate nodes on a giant server.
summaries.advice_en: You can immediately translate these philosophical insights into practice with three concrete actions. First, adopt Rovelli's method of adding tick marks to your days: **do one completely out-of-the-ordinary small thing this weekend to forcefully write fresh temporal anchors into your brain, preventing your months from slipping into a homogeneous blur.** Second, use Libet's and Newton's wisdom to defeat procrastination. Since your internal estimation of time is often a discouraging lie, hand control to an external object—set a twenty-minute timer for a dreaded task and just start, ignoring your brain's anxious prediction that "this will take forever." Finally, establish a one-hour "desynchronization zone" every day: turn off all smart devices with network timestamps and do unstructured activities like walking or Augustine's mental review to reclaim your proper time from the machine's rhythm.

hooks.text: **时间是被谁标准化的**：全球时区不到一百五十年，标准工时更晚，二者都是铁路与工厂的产物；在此之前，隔壁镇的正午与你家的正午本就不是同一刻。我们花整场争论时间是否实在，却很少问它是被谁切成小时、由谁定下起止、又为什么恰好切成这样。若时间的刻度是一项制度，那么『没时间』有多少属于物理，多少属于制度？
hooks.text_en: **Who standardised time**: global time zones are less than a century and a half old, the standard working day younger still, and both are products of railways and factories; before them, noon in the next town simply was not the same moment as noon in yours. We spend a whole debate on whether time is real and rarely ask who cut it into hours, who fixed the start and the end, and why it was cut just so. If the gradations of time are an institution, how much of 'I have no time' is physics and how much is institutional?

hooks.text: **「没时间」不止一种，别用同一副药**：被日程占满、被碎片吞掉、拖延不敢开始、随时被照护打断、一年过去像没发生——这五种说的是同一句话，成因却完全不同，有的要谈判，有的要方法，有的只需要先做十五分钟。先分清自己是哪一种，再谈怎么办。
hooks.text_en: **'I have no time' is not one condition — do not use one remedy**: a calendar taken by others, hours dissolved into fragments, a task you cannot start, a day interrupted by caregiving at any moment, a year that comes back as though it never happened. These five say the same sentence and have nothing in common underneath: some call for negotiation, some for technique, some only for fifteen minutes of starting. Work out which one you have before deciding what to do.

answer.lead: 同一句『我没时间』，底下常是五种完全不同的处境。**先诊断，再下药——搞错种类，再好的方法也只会让人更自责。**

answer.tail: 两条收束：**先分清是『时间被占用』还是『时间感出了问题』——前者要谈判，后者才要方法**；以及，任何要求你更自律的建议，都默认你能支配自己的日程，先看看这个前提在你身上成不成立。

answer_en.lead: One sentence — 'I have no time' — usually covers five quite different situations. **Diagnose before you treat: the wrong category makes even good advice into another reason to blame yourself.**

head: Which kind of 'no time' is yours
Do this first
Why
rows: The calendar really is full, and mostly with things other people put there
Subtract before optimising: pick one thing this week you can decline or hand over, and say so out loud
Practising efficiency on a calendar you do not control books a structural problem to your personal account
You have whole hours, but they dissolve into fragments
Mark two hours a week unbookable, put them in the calendar and tell your colleagues
Focus needs continuity; four half-hours are not one two-hour block
There is time, yet you stall every time you should start
Do fifteen minutes only — and forbid yourself to finish
Procrastination usually jams at the start, not at the length; once you begin, your estimate corrects itself
You are caring for a parent or a small child and can be interrupted at any moment
Negotiate for relief as a necessity, even three hours a week
Interrupted time cannot be repaired by personal technique; it takes someone else taking over

answer_en.tail: Two closing principles: **first work out whether your time is being taken or your sense of time is off — the first calls for negotiation, only the second calls for technique**; and note that every piece of advice demanding more self-discipline assumes you command your own calendar, so check whether that assumption holds in your case.

hooks.text: **若过去与未来同样实在，后悔还剩什么**：块状宇宙常被当成安慰——逝去的人仍在他们那一段里。可同一个图像也指向另一边：若一切已经写定，我们对已发生之恶的愤怒、对未来的努力、对他人的劝告，各自还站得住吗？物理是否真的支持这一步，还是我们把一张几何图误当成了命运？
hooks.text_en: **If past and future are equally real, what is left of regret**: the block universe is usually offered as consolation — those who are gone remain in their stretch of it. But the same picture points the other way: if everything is already written, does our anger at evils already done still stand, and what of effort toward the future, or advice given to another? Does physics actually license that step, or have we mistaken a geometrical diagram for fate?

hooks.text: **我们为什么只记得过去、不记得未来**：这条不对称看似天经地义，其实需要解释——微观定律两个方向都成立，记忆却只朝一边长。若记忆的方向与熵增是同一件事，那『记得』本身就是一种热力学现象；那么改善记忆、修改记忆、乃至一个熵在局部逆转的系统会不会『记得未来』，就都不再是玄想。
hooks.text_en: **Why we remember the past and not the future**: the asymmetry looks self-evident and in fact demands explanation — microscopic laws run either way, yet memory grows in one direction only. If the direction of memory and the growth of entropy are the same fact, then remembering is itself a thermodynamic phenomenon; and improving memory, editing it, or asking whether a system with locally reversed entropy could 'remember forward' all stop being idle speculation.

hooks.text: **童年的夏天为什么那么长**：同一个八月，七岁时无边无际，四十岁时一转眼就过完了。常见的解释是比例（一年占一生的份额越来越小），但也可能是新奇事件的密度、是被安排与自主的差别，或是儿童尚未学会用日程去切割一天。这三种解释给出的对策完全不同——若真想把日子拉长，该复制童年的哪一部分？
hooks.text_en: **Why the summers of childhood were so long**: the same August is boundless at seven and gone in a blink at forty. The usual explanation is proportional — each year is a smaller share of a life — but it could equally be the density of novel events, the difference between a scheduled day and a self-directed one, or simply that a child has not yet learned to cut the day into appointments. The three explanations imply entirely different remedies: if you really want to lengthen your days, which part of childhood should you be copying?

hooks.text: **『我没时间』是陈述还是托辞**：多数时候它描述的不是日程，而是一次不愿承认的排序——说出口的『没时间』，替我们免去了说『这件事排在后面』的难堪。那么在哪些场合它确实是事实，哪些场合它是掩护？若把这句话从词典里删掉、每次都必须说出真正的顺序，我们的生活会更诚实，还是更难以忍受？
hooks.text_en: **'I have no time' — statement or alibi**: most of the time it describes not a calendar but an act of ranking one would rather not admit to; saying it spares us from saying 'this comes lower down my list'. So when is it a plain fact and when is it cover? If the phrase were struck from the language and we had to state the real ordering every time, would our lives become more honest, or merely unbearable?
